uncited: This family encompasses methods that automatically determine the parameters of a transfer function (TF) to match a target visual appearance, optimize feature visibility, or simplify high-dimensional data exploration.
Unlike manual design or static histogram-based generation, these methods treat the TF as an optimization variable or a learned model.

They are distinguished from sibling methods like [Default 3D Transfer Function](5647-default-3d-transfer-function.md) by their reliance on iterative algorithms, neural networks, or sensitivity analysis rather than predefined heuristics or simple statistical clustering.

- [S1] A technique to map nD voxel signatures to continuous 2D (or 3D for spherical maps) map coordinates using Radial Basis Functions, avoiding the discretization error of direct winner-cell assignment.

The evidence explicitly states that to avoid the 'unnecessary discretization' (discretization error) of direct winner-cell assignment, the technique creates 'multiquadric radial basis functions (multiquadric RBFs)' for x and y coordinates (for Kohonen maps) or x, y, and z coordinates (for spherical maps) based on weight vectors. It further confirms that these RBFs are used to 'interpolate' the map coordinates for each nD voxel signature, mapping them to continuous coordinates (0-1 for 2D, -1 to 1 for 3D spherical).
